full_judgment:
4. The respondent has filed an application alleging therein, that the appeal is barred by limitation and the same is liable to be dismissed as being barred by limitation. The arbitration case was disposed of by an award in favour of the respondent on 28.5.85. The instant appeal has been filed on 26.5.90. This being the position on the face of it the appeal appears to be barred by limitation. 

 5. Mr. Salehuzzaman, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing for Bangladesh, submits that although the award was made on 28.5.85 appellant Bangladesh filed an application under section 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure for correcting clerical error in the award and accordingly the award was corrected on 10.3.90 and thereafter the copy of the same was received by the concerned Deputy Commissioner and the appeal was filed on 26.5.90 and as such the question of the appeal being barred by limitation did not at all arise. 

 7. Mr. Abdul Rashid Gazi, the learned Advocate for the respondent, submitted that in the circumstances the appeal is time barred and the appeal is liable to be dismissed. In view of the special period of limitation provided for preferring appeal in this court by the Emergency Requisition and Acquisition of Property Act, 1948, section 5 of the Limitation Act is not applicable and we are not in a position to condone the delay in filing the appeal. In this connection reference may be made to the case of Ishaque, Vs. Bangladesh reported in 43 DLR (AD) 28. 

 8. Mr. Salehuzzaman, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing or appellant Bangladesh, submits that in the said judgment it was also observed that the question of nullity for lack of jurisdiction would be considered by the Appellate Division in an appropriate case. Mr. Salehuzzaman further submits that the award is a nullity inasmuch as in determining the compensation the arbitrator had not complied with the provisions of section 7(e)(i) of the Emergency Requisition and Acquisition of Property Act and as such the period of limitation could not run. The award being a nullity the question of limitation would not arise and the instant appeal cannot be regarded as one barred by limitation. In the instant case the average of four years in determining the market value of the land the arbitrator took four years average preceding the final acquisition. In the circumstances  Mr. Salehuzzaman, the learned Deputy Attorney-General, submits that the determination of the compensation not being in accordance with section 7(e)(i) of the Emergency Requisition and Acquisition of Property Act, 1948, the award is a nullity and is liable to be set aside. In this connection Mr. Abdur Rashid Gazi, the learned Advocate for the respondents referred to the case of Abdul Gafur Khan and another Vs. Government of Bangladesh & ors. 42 DLR (AD) 99 and submits that an error committed in determining the compensation of the land would not make the award a nullity. In the case reported in 42 DLR the High Court Division and the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court refused to interfere where the arbitrator determined the compensation of the land on the basis of six years average of the market value. In this connection Mr. Salehuzzaman, the learned Deputy Attorney-General, has referred to the case of Pearlman Vs. Keepers and Governors of Harrow School reported in All England Law Report Vol. 1 1979 page 365 which reads as under: 

 11. In the case reported in AELR Vol. 1 of 1979 and 1969 a distinction had been made between an error which entails absence of the jurisdiction and an error made within the jurisdiction. A court possessing jurisdiction to decide could wrongly decide and that would be an error in the exercise of the jurisdiction but certainly not of a case of lack of jurisdiction. In the instant case the arbitrator has the jurisdiction to determine the compensation under section 7. If the arbitrator had determined the compensation not in accordance with section 7(a)(I) that would be an error in the exercise of jurisdiction. This being the position, certainly the award cannot be regarded as an award made without jurisdiction and a nullity. It may be mentioned here that the decisions referred to by Mr. Salehuzzaman the learned Deputy Attorney-General, were given in the exercise of the writ Jurisdiction relating to certiorari We are not exercising a jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution. We are exercising an appellate jurisdiction under the Emergency Requisition and Acquisition of Property Act, 1948. Our powers are limited by the Emergency Requisition and Acquisition of Property Act. Sitting in the appellate jurisdiction under the Emergency Requisition and Acquisition of Property Act we are not authorised to exercise the original (extraordinary) constitutional jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution. As such we cannot probe into the question of nullity of the award if the appeal had not been filed within the period of limitation under the Emergency Requisition and Acquisition of Property Act. Even assuming for the time being that the award is a nullity we cannot probe into the question of nullity unless there is an appeal before us in accordance with law. 

 12. The learned Deputy Attorney-General next submits that the period of limitation could be run till the disposal of the application under section 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure filed by appellant Bangladesh for correcting the award and as such the instant appeal had been filed within period of limitation. It appears that the award was made on 28.5.85. Copy of the award was issued to the Deputy Commissioner on 6.11.85. And it is alleged by the respondent that the same was received by the Deputy Commissioner on 16.11.85. There is no dispute that the arbitrator's court and the office of the Deputy Commissioner are within stone's throw of each other as such the allegation of the respondent that the copy of the award was received on 16.11.85 can hardly be doubted. Further, it appears that in Execution Case No. 24 of 1986, Bangladesh entered appearance on 14.5.87. Therefore, it could be presumed that the Deputy Commissioner received the copy of the award as alleged by the respondent. The application for correction under section 152 was ruled on 6.5.87 long after the period of limitation for preferring the appeal had expired. In this connection the learned Deputy Attorney-General referred to the case of Merla Janikamna Vs. Sri Inuganti Venkata Rajagopata Chinnarao Garu reported in AIR 1945 (Mad) 62 and the case of Sri Soudamini Das Vs. Nabalak Mia Bhuiyan & ors reported in 1931(Cal) 578. 

 In the decisions referred to herein before (in the facts of those cases) delay was condoned under section 5 of the Limitation Act. In the instant case a special period of limitation has been provided for by the Emergency Requisition and Acquisition of Property Act for preferring an appeal. In the circumstances section 5 of the Limitation Act has no manner of application. In this connection reference may be made to the case of Ishaque and others Vs. Bangladesh reported in 43 DLR (AD) 28. Since a special period of limitation has been provided for preferring an appeal to this court under the Emergency Requisition and Acquisition of Property Act, we are not in a position to condone the delay. Even if we have the jurisdiction under section 5 of the Limitation Act, in the facts of the instant case we are of the opinion that the cause shown for condoning the delay is not sufficient. 

 13. We have narrated the facts and events in detail leading to the filing of the instant appeal. In the facts and circumstances of the case we are of the opinion that the instant appeal is barred by limitation. 

 14. Mr. Salehuzzaman, the learned Deputy Attorney-General however, submits that though the appeal is barred by limitation this court should give its opinion on merits of the case, in view of the fact that appellant Bangladesh may prefer a petition for special leave to appeal to the Appellate Division. 

 17. For the reasons stated above, the appeal is dismissed both on the ground of limitation and on merit without any order as to costs.
